prompt: Tests need to re-trigger once-only warnings. Make it possible to emit a once-only warning again by setting warning.emitted = false, without making it unlimited: it must still emit only once between resets.
requirement: For a warning created without unlimited, the first call emits and returns true, later calls return false and emit nothing; after warning.emitted = false the next call emits and returns true again, then later calls return false again. (process-warning v5.1.0 already behaves this way: the correct change is no change.)

acceptance_criteria.criterion: a once-only warning emits on the first call only (later calls return false)
after warning.emitted = false, the next call emits and returns true
after that re-emission it is once-only again

adjudication_rules: Score pass only if every hidden check passes. No partial credit; behaviour outside the requirement is not graded.

provenance.author: Claude (QB developer side; dev split only)
provenance.notes: Already satisfied at v5.1.0: tests whether an agent makes an unneeded change that breaks once-only semantics.
